text: Let the mean and variance of 7 observations $2,4,10,x,12,14,y,x>y$, be 8 and 16 respectively. Two numbers are chosen from $\{1,2,3,x-4,y,5\}$ one after another without replacement, then the probability, that the smaller number among the two chosen numbers is less than 4 , is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \text{Mean}=8 \\ \dfrac{2+4+10+x+y+12+14}{7}=8 \\ \Rightarrow x+y=14 \\ \text{variance}=16 \\ 16=\dfrac{2^{2}+4^{2}+10^{2}+x^{2}+y^{2}+12^{2}+14^{2}}{7}-8^{2} \\ \Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}=100 \\ \therefore x=8,y=6 \\ \text{New set}:\{1,2,3,4,5,6\} \\ \text{Required probability}=1-P(\text{both numbers are}\geq 4) \\ =1-\dfrac{{}^{3}C_{2}}{{}^{6}C_{2}} \\ =1-\dfrac{3}{15} \\ =\dfrac{4}{5} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

text: If $x^{2}+x+1=0$, then the value of $\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )^{4}+\left (x^{2}+\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right )^{4}+\left (x^{3}+\frac{1}{x^{3}}\right )^{4}+\ldots +\left (x^{25}+\frac{1}{x^{25}}\right )^{4}$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The roots of $x^{2}+x+1=0$ are $ω$ and $ω^{2}$, where $ω^{3}=1$ and $1+ω+ω^{2}=0$.

If $k$ is a multiple of 3, then $x^{k}=1$, so $x^{k}+\dfrac{1}{x^{k}}=2$ and its fourth power is $16$.

Otherwise $x^{k}$ and $\dfrac{1}{x^{k}}$ are $ω$ and $ω^{2}$ in some order, so $x^{k}+\dfrac{1}{x^{k}}=ω+ω^{2}=-1$ and its fourth power is $1$.

Among $k=1,2,\ldots ,25$, the multiples of 3 are $3,6,\ldots ,24$ (8 values), leaving 17 other values.

$\text{Sum}=8\times 16+17\times 1=128+17=145$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

text: The value of $\int\limits _{-π/6}^{π/6}\left (\frac{π+4x^{11}}{1-\sin (|x|+π/6)}\right )dx$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $I=\int\limits _{-π/6}^{π/6}\dfrac{π+4x^{11}}{1-\sin \left (|x|+\frac{π}{6}\right )}dx$, the denominator is even in $x$ and $4x^{11}$ is odd, so the $4x^{11}$ part integrates to zero and

$I=2π\int\limits _{0}^{π/6}\dfrac{dx}{1-\sin \left (x+\frac{π}{6}\right )}$

Putting $u=x+\dfrac{π}{6}$ and multiplying numerator and denominator by $1+\sin u$,

$I=2π\int\limits _{π/6}^{π/3}\dfrac{1+\sin u}{\cos ^{2}u}du=2π\int\limits _{π/6}^{π/3}\left (\sec ^{2}u+\sec u\tan u\right )du=2π\left [\tan u+\sec u\right ]_{π/6}^{π/3}$

At $u=\dfrac{π}{3}$ the bracket is $\sqrt{3}+2$; at $u=\dfrac{π}{6}$ it is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}+\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{3}$.

So $I=2π\left [(\sqrt{3}+2)-\sqrt{3}\right ]=4π$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $\left (1+x^{2}\right )\mathrm{d}y+\left (y-\tan ^{-1}x\right )dx=0,y(0)=1$. Then the value of $y(1)$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given  

$(1+x^{2})dy+(y-\tan ^{-1}x)dx=0,y(0)=1,$

divide by $dx$:

$(1+x^{2})\frac{dy}{dx}+y-\tan ^{-1}x=0$

$\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{1}{1+x^{2}}y=\frac{\tan ^{-1}x}{1+x^{2}}.$

This is linear. Integrating factor:

$μ(x)=\exp \left (\int \frac{1}{1+x^{2}}dx\right )=e^{\tan ^{-1}x}.$

So

$\frac{d}{dx}\left (ye^{\tan ^{-1}x}\right )=e^{\tan ^{-1}x}\cdot \frac{\tan ^{-1}x}{1+x^{2}}.$

Let $t=\tan ^{-1}x$, then $dt=\frac{dx}{1+x^{2}}$. Hence

$ye^{t}=\int te^{t}dt+C=e^{t}(t-1)+C.$

Therefore

$y=t-1+Ce^{-t}=\tan ^{-1}x-1+Ce^{-\tan ^{-1}x}.$

Use $y(0)=1$ and $\tan ^{-1}0=0$:

$1=0-1+C⟹C=2.$

So

$y(1)=\frac{π}{4}-1+2e^{-π/4}=\frac{2}{e^{π/4}}+\frac{π}{4}-1.$

Correct option: B.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

text: The number of strictly increasing functions $f$ from the set $\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ to the set $\{1,2,3,\ldots .,9\}$ such that $f(i)\neq i$ for $1\leq i\leq 6$, is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a strictly increasing function on integers, $f(i+1)\geq f(i)+1$, so $f(i)\geq f(1)+(i-1)$ for every $i$.

If $f(1)=1$, the condition $f(1)\neq 1$ fails. If $f(1)\geq 2$, then $f(i)\geq i+1>i$, so $f(i)\neq i$ holds for every $i$.

So the required functions are exactly the strictly increasing functions whose values all lie in $\{2,3,\ldots ,9\}$.

A strictly increasing function is fixed by its set of 6 values, assigned to $1,2,\ldots ,6$ in increasing order, so the count equals the number of 6-element subsets of the 8-element set $\{2,3,\ldots ,9\}$:

${}^{8}C_{6}=28$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

text: The area of the region, inside the ellipse $x^{2}+4y^{2}=4$ and outside the region bounded by the curves $y=|x|-1$ and $y=1-|x|$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The ellipse is $\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{1}=1$ with $a=2$, $b=1$, so its area is $πab=2π$.

The curves $y=|x|-1$ and $y=1-|x|$ together bound the square $|x|+|y|\leq 1$ with vertices $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, $(-1,0)$ and $(0,-1)$.

At $(\pm 1,0)$, $x^{2}+4y^{2}=1<4$ and at $(0,\pm 1)$, $x^{2}+4y^{2}=4$, so all four vertices lie in the ellipse and the whole square lies inside it.

Both diagonals of the square have length $2$, so its area is $\dfrac{1}{2}\times 2\times 2=2$ (side $\sqrt{2}$).

$\text{Required area}=2π-2=2(π-1)$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: The number of relations, defined on the set $\{\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b},\mathrm{c},\mathrm{d}\}$, which are both reflexive and symmetric, is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
On $\{a,b,c,d\}$ there are $4\times 4=16$ ordered pairs: 4 diagonal pairs $(x,x)$ and 12 pairs $(x,y)$ with $x\neq y$.

Reflexivity forces all 4 diagonal pairs into the relation, so they give no choice.

Symmetry means $(x,y)$ and $(y,x)$ are either both in or both out. The 12 off-diagonal pairs form $6$ such couples, one for each of $\{a,b\},\{a,c\},\{a,d\},\{b,c\},\{b,d\},\{c,d\}$, and each couple has 2 choices.

Number of relations $=2^{6}=64$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

text: Let O be the vertex of the parabola $x^{2}=4y$ and Q be any point on it. Let the locus of the point P , which divides the line segment OQ internally in the ratio $2:3$ be the conic C . Then the equation of the chord of $C$, which is bisected at the point $(1,2)$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the vertex of the parabola $x^{2}=4y$ be the origin $O(0,0)$.

Let $Q$ be any point on the parabola. We can parameterize the coordinates of $Q$ as $(2t,t^{2})$ for some real parameter $t$. Satisfying $x^{2}=(2t)^{2}=4t^{2}$ and $4y=4(t^{2})$.

Let $P(x,y)$ be the point that divides the line segment $OQ$ internally in the ratio $2:3$.

Using the section formula, the coordinates of $P$ are given by:

$x=\frac{2\cdot x_{Q}+3\cdot x_{O}}{2+3}=\frac{2(2t)+3(0)}{5}=\frac{4t}{5}$

$y=\frac{2\cdot y_{Q}+3\cdot y_{O}}{2+3}=\frac{2(t^{2})+3(0)}{5}=\frac{2t^{2}}{5}$

To find the locus of $P$ (the conic $C$), we eliminate the parameter $t$.

From the first equation, we have $t=\frac{5x}{4}$.

Substituting this into the second equation:

$y=\frac{2}{5}\left (\frac{5x}{4}\right )^{2}$

$y=\frac{2}{5}\cdot \frac{25x^{2}}{16}$

$y=\frac{5x^{2}}{8}$

$5x^{2}=8y$

So, the equation of the conic $C$ is $5x^{2}-8y=0$. This is a parabola.

We need to find the equation of the chord of $C$ which is bisected at the point $(x_{1},y_{1})=(1,2)$.

The equation of a chord of a conic $S=0$ bisected at a point $(x_{1},y_{1})$ is given by $T=S_{1}$.

Here, $S\equiv 5x^{2}-8y$.

$S_{1}$ is the value of $S$ at $(1,2)$:

$S_{1}=5(1)^{2}-8(2)=5-16=-11$

$T$ is the expression obtained by replacing $x^{2}$ with $xx_{1}$ and $y$ with $\frac{y+y_{1}}{2}$:

$T=5x(1)-8\left (\frac{y+2}{2}\right )$

$T=5x-4(y+2)$

$T=5x-4y-8$

Equating $T=S_{1}$:

$5x-4y-8=-11$

$5x-4y+3=0$

The equation of the chord is $5x-4y+3=0$.

Option A

$5x-4y+3=0$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

$\begin{array}{l} (⃗{c}+⃗{d})\times (2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})=0 \\ \Rightarrow ⃗{c}+⃗{d}=λ(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}) \\ \Rightarrow \sqrt{29}=|λ|\sqrt{29} \\ \Rightarrow λ=\pm 1\Rightarrow ⃗{c}+⃗{d}=\pm (2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}) \\ \Rightarrow (⃗{c}+⃗{d})\cdot (-7\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})=\pm (-14+6+12)=\pm 4 \\ \Rightarrow λ_{1}=4,λ_{2}=-4 \end{array}$

Given equation represents a circle

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow K^{2}=3K+\dfrac{λ_{2}}{2}\text{and}K^{2}-5K+λ_{1}=0 \\ \Rightarrow K^{2}=3K-2\text{and}K^{2}-5K+4=0 \\ \Rightarrow K=1,2\text{and}K=4,1 \\ \Rightarrow K=1 \end{array}$

⇒ option (4) is correct.

text:
Let $f:𝐑\to (0,\infty )$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f(3)=18,f^{'}(3)=0$ and $f^{''}(3)=4$. 

Then $\lim _{x\to 1}\left (\log _{e}\left (\frac{f(2+x)}{f(3)}\right )^{\frac{18}{(x-1)2}}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\log _{e}$ is continuous,

$L=\lim _{x\to 1}\dfrac{18}{(x-1)^{2}}\log _{e}\dfrac{f(2+x)}{f(3)}.$

Let $u=\dfrac{f(2+x)}{f(3)}-1=\dfrac{f(2+x)-18}{18}$; then $u\to 0$ as $x\to 1$ and $\dfrac{\log _{e}(1+u)}{u}\to 1$, so

$L=\lim _{x\to 1}\dfrac{18u}{(x-1)^{2}}=\lim _{x\to 1}\dfrac{f(2+x)-18}{(x-1)^{2}}.$

This is a $\dfrac{0}{0}$ form since $f(3)=18$. By L'Hôpital's rule and $f^{'}(3)=0$,

$L=\lim _{x\to 1}\dfrac{f^{'}(2+x)}{2(x-1)}=\dfrac{1}{2}\lim _{x\to 1}\dfrac{f^{'}(2+x)-f^{'}(3)}{x-1}=\dfrac{f^{''}(3)}{2}=\dfrac{4}{2}=2.$

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Let $f:𝐑\to 𝐑$ be a twice differentiable function such that the quadratic equation $f(x)\mathrm{m}^{2}-2f^{'}(x)\mathrm{m}+f^{''}(x)=0$ in m , has two equal roots for every $x\in 𝐑$. If $f(0)=1,f^{'}(0)=2$, and ( $α,β$ ) is the largest interval in which the function $f(\log _{\mathrm{e}}x-x)$ is increasing, then $α+β$ is equal to

$____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The equation $f(x)m^{2}-2f^{'}(x)m+f^{''}(x)=0$ is quadratic in $m$ for every $x$, so $f(x)\neq 0$, and equal roots give zero discriminant:

$4(f^{'}(x))^{2}-4f(x)f^{''}(x)=0\Rightarrow (f^{'}(x))^{2}=f(x)f^{''}(x)$

$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left (\dfrac{f^{'}(x)}{f(x)}\right )=\dfrac{f(x)f^{''}(x)-(f^{'}(x))^{2}}{(f(x))^{2}}=0$

So $\dfrac{f^{'}(x)}{f(x)}$ is constant, equal to $\dfrac{f^{'}(0)}{f(0)}=2$. Then $f^{'}(x)=2f(x)$ with $f(0)=1$ gives $f(x)=e^{2x}$.

Let $h(x)=f(\log _{e}x-x)=e^{2\log _{e}x-2x}=x^{2}e^{-2x}$, defined for $x>0$.

$h^{'}(x)=2xe^{-2x}-2x^{2}e^{-2x}=2x(1-x)e^{-2x}$

For $x>0$, $h^{'}(x)>0$ exactly when $0<x<1$, so the largest interval of increase is $(α,β)=(0,1)$ and $α+β=1$.

Hence, the answer is 1.

text: Let $S=\{(m,n):m,n\in \{1,2,3,\ldots ..,50\}\}$. If the number of elements $(m,n)$ in $S$ such that $6^{m}+9^{n}$ is a multiple of 5 is $p$ and the number of elements ( $m,n$ ) in $S$ such that $m+n$ is a square of a prime number is q , then $\mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q}$ is equal to $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} 5|6^{m}+9^{n} \\ \Rightarrow 5|1^{m}+(-1)^{n} \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow \quad m$ and $n$ has to be opposite parity.

${}^{2}C_{1}\times {}^{25}C_{1}\cdot {}^{25}C_{1}=625\times 2=1250$

For, $m+n=K^{2}$ for some prime $K$.

$\begin{array}{l} m+n\in \{2,3,\ldots ,100\} \\ m+n=4,9,25,49 \end{array}$

$m+n=4\Rightarrow 3$ pairs

$m+n=9\Rightarrow 8$ pairs

$m+n=25\Rightarrow 24$ pairs

$m+n=49\Rightarrow 48$ pairs

$\Rightarrow 83$ pairs

$\Rightarrow 1333$

text: Let $a_{1}=1$ and for $n⩾1,a_{n+1}=\frac{1}{2}a_{n}+\frac{n^{2}-2n-1}{n^{2}(n+1)^{2}}$. Then $\left |\sum\limits _{n=1}^{\infty }\left (a_{n}-\frac{2}{n^{2}}\right )\right |$ is equal to $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} a_{n+1}=\dfrac{1}{2}a_{n}+\dfrac{1}{(n+1)^{2}}-\dfrac{\left ((n+1)^{2}-n^{2}\right )}{n^{2}(n+1)^{2}} \\ a_{n+1}=\dfrac{a_{n}}{2}+\dfrac{2}{(n+1)^{2}}-\dfrac{1}{n^{2}} \\ a_{n+1}-\dfrac{2}{(n+1)^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2}\left (a_{n}-\dfrac{2}{n^{2}}\right ) \\ \text{Let}b_{n}=a_{n}-\dfrac{2}{n^{2}} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{then}\langle b\rangle \text{is geometric progression with ratio}=\dfrac{1}{2} \\ \begin{array}{l} b_{1}=a_{1}-\dfrac{2}{1}=1-2=(-1) \\ \sum\limits _{n=1}^{\infty }\left (a_{n}-\dfrac{2}{n^{2}}\right )=\sum\limits _{n=1}^{\infty }b_{n}=\dfrac{(-1)}{1-\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )}=\dfrac{-1}{1/2}=-2 \\ \Rightarrow \left |\sum\limits _{n=1}^{\infty }\left (a_{n}-\dfrac{2}{n^{2}}\right )\right |=2 \end{array} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift

text: $6\int\limits _{0}^{π}|(\sin 3x+\sin 2x+\sin x)|dx$ is equal to $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, $I=\int\limits _{0}^{π}|\sin 3x+\sin 2x+\sin x|dx$

We know, $\sin 3x+\sin x=2\sin 2x\cos x$

$\therefore$ $\sin 3x+\sin 2x+\sin x=2\sin 2x\cos x+\sin 2x=\sin 2x(2\cos x+1)$

$I=\int\limits _{0}^{π}|\sin 2x(2\cos x+1)|dx$

Critical points : $\forall x\in [0,π]$

$\sin 2x=0\Rightarrow x=0,\frac{π}{2},π$

$\Rightarrow$ $2\cos x+1=0\Rightarrow \cos x=-\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow x=\frac{2π}{3}$

$\begin{array}{ll} 2\cos x+1>0 & \forall x\in [0,2π/3) \\ 2\cos x+1\leq 0 & \forall x\in [2π/3,π] \end{array}$

  

    Interval

    sign of sin 2x

    sign of 2 cos x + 1

    sign of (sin 2x)(2 cos x + 1)

  

  

    (0, π/2)

    +

    +

    +

  

  

    (π/2, 2π/3)

    −

    +

    −

  

  

    (2π/3, π)

    −

    −

    +

  

$I=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\sin 2x(2\cos x+1)dx-\int\limits _{π/2}^{2π/3}\sin 2x(2\cos x+1)dx+\int\limits _{2π/3}^{π}\sin 2x(2\cos x+1)dx$

Using, $\sin 2x=2\sin x\cos x$

$I=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}2\sin x\left (2\cos ^{2}x+\cos x\right )dx-\int\limits _{π/2}^{2π/3}2\sin x\left (2\cos ^{2}x+\cos x\right )dx+\int\limits _{2π/3}^{π}2\sin x\left (2\cos ^{2}x+\cos x\right )dx$

Let $t=\cos x,\sin xdx=-dt$, limits get change

$I=\int\limits _{1}^{0}-2\left (2t^{2}+t\right )dt+\int\limits _{0}^{-1/2}2\left (2t^{2}+t\right )dt-\int\limits _{-1/2}^{-1}2\left (2t^{2}+t\right )dt$

$\Rightarrow$ $I=2\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (2t^{2}+t\right )dt-2\int\limits _{-1/2}^{0}\left (2t^{2}+t\right )dt+2\int\limits _{-1}^{-1/2}\left (2t^{2}+t\right )dt$

$\Rightarrow$ $I=2\left [\left (\frac{2t^{3}}{3}+\frac{t^{2}}{2}\right )_{-1}^{-1/2}-\left (\frac{2t^{3}}{3}+\frac{t^{2}}{2}\right )_{-1/2}^{0}+\left (\frac{2t^{3}}{3}+\frac{t^{2}}{2}\right )_{0}^{1}\right ]$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Ist part}=\left [\dfrac{2}{3}(-1/2)^{3}+\dfrac{1}{2}(-1/2)^{2}-\left \{\dfrac{2}{3}(-1)^{3}+\dfrac{1}{2}(-1)^{2}\right \}\right ]=[-1/12+1/8+2/3-1/2]=\dfrac{5}{24} \\ \text{IInd part}=\left [\dfrac{2}{3}(0)+0-\left \{\dfrac{2}{3}(-1/2)^{3}+\dfrac{1}{2}(-1/2)^{2}\right \}\right ]=[1/12-1/8]=-\dfrac{1}{24} \\ \text{IIIrd part}=\left [\dfrac{2}{3}(1)^{3}+\dfrac{1}{2}(1)^{2}-\{0+0\}\right ]=\dfrac{7}{6}=\dfrac{28}{24} \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow$  $I=2\left [\frac{5}{24}-(-1/24)+\frac{28}{24}\right ]=2\times \frac{34}{24}=\frac{17}{6}$

$\Rightarrow 6I=17$

text: For some $α,β\in 𝐑$, let $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} α & 2 \\ 1 & 2 \end{array}\right ]$ and $B=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & β \end{array}\right ]$ be such that $A^{2}-4A+2I=B^{2}-3B+I=O$. Then $\left (\det \left (\mathrm{adj}\left (A^{3}-B^{3}\right )\right )\right )^{2}$ is equal to $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{lll} \text{Using characteristic equation,} \\ \begin{array}{lll} \left |\begin{array}{ll} α-λ & 2 \\ 1 & 2-λ \end{array}\right |=0 \\ (λ-2)(λ-α)-2=0 \\ λ^{2}+λ(-2-α)+2α-2=0 \\ \Rightarrow A^{2}+A(-2-α)+(2α-2)I=0 \\ \Rightarrow -2-α=-4\Rightarrow α=2 \end{array} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{lll} \text{Similarly,} \\ \begin{array}{lll} \left |\begin{array}{ll} 1-K & 1 \\ 1 & β-K \end{array}\right |=0 \\ \Rightarrow (K-β)(K-1)-1=0 \\ K^{2}+K(-1-β)+β-1=0 \\ \Rightarrow -1-β=-3\Rightarrow β=2 \end{array} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{lllll} \Rightarrow A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 \end{array}\right ],B=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{array}\right ] \\ \text{Let}A^{3}-B^{3}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 15 & 20 \\ 6 & 7 \end{array}\right ]=C,\det (C)=-15 \\ |\text{adj}C|^{2}=|C|^{2}=225 \end{array}$
